newsitem.title: PERU: Peruvians approve Fujimori's crisis handling - poll.
newsitem.headline: Peruvians approve Fujimori's crisis handling - poll.

text.p: A majority of Peruvians approve of President Alberto Fujimori's handling of the five-week hostage crisis, a leading pollster said on Tuesday.
The Apoyo survey of 900 people showed 59 percent thought Fujimori had done a good job, while 30 percent disapproved.

The Dec. 17 takeover of the Japanese ambassador's residence by Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels, who still hold 73 VIP hostages, has presented Fujimori with the worst crisis of his six years in office.
A minority of 19 percent of Peruvians believe Fujimori should order a military storming of the residence, while 75 percent want the government to seek a negotiated solution.

To achieve the freedom of the hostages, 76 percent think the government should agree to improve the conditions of MRTA leaders in jail, while 67 percent think the hostage-takers should be allowed to escape to a foreign country, Apoyo said.
Only 10 percent agreed with the MRTA's main demand of freedom for some 400 jailed comrades.
Fujimori's popularity has crept up during the crisis to 47 percent in January from 45 percent in December, Apoyo added.
